posts.title: UK Non-Dom Abolition: Your Paraguay Exit Strategy for 2026
posts.excerpt: The UK abolished its non-dom regime on April 6, 2025. Worldwide income is now taxed on the arising basis with a 10-year IHT tail. Here is why Paraguay is the most compelling alternative for the 16,500 millionaires expected to leave Britain this year.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
The UK non-dom regime is dead. As of April 6, 2025, the remittance basis that allowed non-domiciled residents to avoid UK tax on foreign income and gains is gone. Worldwide income is now taxed on the arising basis from day one.

Henley & Partners projects **16,500 millionaires will leave the UK in 2025** — the highest outflow of any country globally. This is not a trickle. This is a door slamming shut.

## What Actually Changed

| Before April 2025 | After April 2025 |
|---|---|
| Non-doms could claim remittance basis — only UK income taxed | Remittance basis abolished entirely |
| Foreign income and gains exempt if not brought to UK | All worldwide income taxed on arising basis |
| IHT only on UK assets | IHT on worldwide assets after 10 years of residence |
| Simple to leave | New 10-year IHT tail follows you |

The new Foreign Income and Gains (FIG) regime offers a temporary 4-year exemption for new arrivals, but for existing residents there is no transition — the change is immediate and unforgiving.

## Where Do You Go?

The traditional alternatives have their own problems in 2026:

**Gibraltar — Cat 2 Status**
- Maximum tax capped at £42,000/year
- Housing crisis, severely limited availability
- OECD pressure making the regime less attractive
- No path to citizenship

**UAE — Dubai**
- True 0% income tax
- Cost of living 2-3x higher than Paraguay (Dubai 1BR: £1,500-2,500/mo)
- **No path to citizenship** — naturalisation only by sovereign decree after 30+ years
- You are always a temporary resident

**Portugal D7**
- NHR regime ended January 2024
- Foreign income now taxed up to **48%**
- Requires 183 days/year physical presence
- 5 years to citizenship, but at enormous tax cost

**Spain Non-Lucrative Visa**
- 47% income tax rate
- Wealth tax on global assets over €700K
- **Cannot work at all** — even remote work is restricted
- 10 years to citizenship

## Why Paraguay

Paraguay offers something none of the above can match in 2026:

| Factor | Paraguay |
|---|---|
| Foreign income tax | **0%** — permanently, by law, no sunset |
| Local income tax | 10% flat (only on Paraguay-source income) |
| Wealth tax | **None** |
| Inheritance tax | **None** |
| Physical presence | **1 visit every 3 years** |
| Citizenship | **3 years** (fastest in the western hemisphere) |
| Cost of living | £900-1,200/month for a couple |
| CRS reporting | **No** — Paraguay does not participate |
| Work allowed | Yes (with RUC — simple registration) |

## The Numbers

A UK resident with £2M in investment assets earning £80,000/year in passive income:

**Stay in the UK:**
- Income tax on £80K: ~£27,000
- IHT exposure on £2M estate: £800,000 at death
- **Total annual tax: ~£27,000**

**Move to Paraguay:**
- Foreign income tax: **£0**
- Wealth tax: **£0**
- IHT: **£0**
- **Total annual tax: ~£0**

**Annual saving: £27,000. Lifetime IHT saving: £800,000.**

## What About the IHT Tail?

The new rules create a 10-year IHT tail for UK residents who leave. This means your worldwide assets remain within UK IHT for 10 years after departure. It is real. It requires planning.

However:
- After 10 years, you are fully free of UK IHT
- Paraguay has **no inheritance tax** — so in year 11+, your estate faces zero tax in both jurisdictions
- The IHT tail is temporary; Paraguay's 0% is permanent

## Next Steps

The window for proactive planning is now. Every month you wait is another month of tax on worldwide income you could keep.

Agenda a free 30-minute consultation with our team. We will map your specific UK tax situation, explain the SRT (Statutory Residence Test), and show you exactly what Paraguay residency would mean for your numbers.

posts.title: Paraguay vs Portugal for UK Expats in 2026: The Honest Comparison
posts.excerpt: Portugal was the #1 relocation destination for UK expats. Then the NHR regime died. Here is the honest, side-by-side comparison of Paraguay vs Portugal for residency, tax, citizenship, and cost of living in 2026.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
For a decade, Portugal was the default answer for any UK expat looking for a European exit. The Non-Habitual Resident (NHR) regime offered 10 years of 10% tax on foreign pensions and 0% on most foreign income — all while living in the sun with EU passport access.

That era ended in January 2024. And the alternatives in 2026 look very different.

## The Head-to-Head

| Factor | Paraguay | Portugal |
|---|---|---|
| **Foreign income tax** | **0%** — permanent, by law | Up to **48%** progressive (NHR dead) |
| **Local income tax** | 10% flat | 14.5-48% progressive |
| **Wealth tax** | None | None (but AIMI 0.4-0.7% on property >€600K) |
| **Minimum income** | **$0** | €8,460/yr (D7) or €3,280/mo (D8) |
| **Physical presence** | **1 visit every 3 years** | 183 days/year strictly enforced |
| **Citizenship** | **3 years** | 5 years (with A2 Portuguese test) |
| **Passport power** | ~145 countries visa-free | ~189 countries (EU) |
| **Cost of living (couple)** | **£900-1,200/mo** | £2,000-3,000/mo |
| **CRS reporting** | **No** | Yes (full EU transparency) |
| **Work allowed** | Yes (with RUC) | Yes (D8, but restricted D7) |

## What Changed in Portugal

The NHR regime was officially closed to new applicants from January 1, 2024. The replacement, the IFICI regime, only benefits researchers, scientists, and tech professionals. For everyone else:

- Pensions are now taxed at progressive **Portuguese rates up to 48%**
- Foreign dividends and rental income: **28% flat**
- Foreign employment income: **progressive up to 48%**
- No more 10-year holiday

The Portugal dream for tax optimizers is over.

## The Tax Numbers: A Real Example

UK expat with £50,000/year in UK pension income:

**Portugal D7:**
- Pension taxed at progressive rates: ~£12,000/year in tax
- Requires 183 days/year in-country
- Must rent or buy property (Lisbon 1BR: £800+/mo)
- **Net after tax and housing: ~£24,000/year**

**Paraguay:**
- Pension taxed: **£0** (foreign income, territorial system)
- Requires 1 visit every 3 years
- Cost of living for a couple: £900-1,200/mo all-in
- **Net after tax and housing: ~£36,000/year**

**Difference: £12,000 more disposable income per year in Paraguay.**

## The One Real Advantage Portugal Still Has

The EU passport. Portugal gives you citizenship in 5 years and with it, the right to live, work, and retire anywhere in the EU. It is the most powerful passport in the world.

Paraguay's passport gives visa-free access to ~145 countries including the entire Schengen zone (90 days), UK, and most of Latin America — but not the right to live in the EU.

**When Portugal still wins:** You need EU freedom of movement, you have family in Europe, or your income is low enough that the tax difference is small.

**When Paraguay wins:** You care about keeping your money, you do not need to live in Europe full-time, or the tax saving exceeds the value of an EU passport.

## The Hidden Costs of Portugal

| Cost | Portugal | Paraguay |
|---|---|---|
| NHR is dead | Pension taxed up to 48% | 0% on foreign income |
| Mandatory presence | 183 days/year | 1 visit/3 years |
| Property costs (buying) | 6-8% transaction tax | 2-3% total |
| Property costs (renting) | Lisbon 1BR: £800-1,200 | Asunción 1BR: £300-400 |
| Healthcare | Public + mandatory private | Private insurance £40-120/mo |
| Banking | CRS reported to HMRC | No CRS reporting |
| Exit after 5+ years | May face exit tax if Citizenship not secured | Clear exit, no penalties |

## When Paraguay Makes Sense for UK Expats

- Your primary goal is **tax optimization** — keep more of your pension, investment, or business income
- You are **not required to live in Europe full-time** — you want flexibility
- You want **fast citizenship** — Paraguay grants it in 3 years, Portugal in 5-6
- You want **permanent residency from day one** — Portugal starts with temporary renewable visas
- You want **no physical presence requirement** — you travel, you have a second home elsewhere

## When Portugal Still Makes Sense

- EU citizenship is non-negotiable and you are willing to pay the 48% tax to get it
- You need proximity to family in Europe
- You require European healthcare infrastructure
- Your income is modest and the tax difference is small

## The Verdict

In 2026, the question is no longer "Portugal or Paraguay?" for the UK expat. The question is: **"Is an EU passport worth paying 48% tax for the next 5 years?"**

For most UK expats with meaningful savings or pensions, the answer is no. Paraguay saves you tens of thousands of pounds per year, gives you a path to citizenship in less time, and requires almost nothing from you in terms of physical presence.

Come talk to us. We will run your numbers side by side — Portugal vs Paraguay — so you can decide on data, not marketing.

posts.title: DAC8 is Live: Europe's Crypto Reporting Law and Why Paraguay Is the Escape Route
posts.excerpt: DAC8 went live January 2026. All EU crypto exchanges now report holdings and transactions to your local tax authority. For crypto investors in Europe, this changes everything. Here is why Paraguay is the most compelling option for a crypto tax exit.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
January 2026 marked a turning point for crypto investors in Europe. DAC8 — the EU's eighth Directive on Administrative Cooperation — went live, and with it, the era of anonymous crypto holdings in Europe is over.

## What DAC8 Does

From January 1, 2026, all crypto-asset service providers registered in the EU are required to:

- Report every customer's **transactions, holdings, and gains** to their home tax authority
- Automatically exchange this data with all other EU member states
- Report **historical data** going back to January 2023
- Cover all crypto-assets: Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, DeFi tokens, NFTs

The reporting is granular, automated, and mutual. Your crypto portfolio is no longer private from your tax authority.

## What This Means by Country

| Country | Crypto Tax Rate | Current Impact of DAC8 |
|---|---|---|
| Netherlands | **36% on unrealised gains** (Box 3, from 2028) | Massive — being taxed on gains you have not realised |
| Germany | 26.375% on gains <1yr held, **0% after 1yr** | Worst for traders and stakers |
| Spain | 19-28% on gains (sliding scale) | + wealth tax on global assets over €700K |
| France | 30% flat (PFU) | Simple but high — 30% on every trade |
| Italy | **33% from 2026** (up from 26%) | Regulatory tightening + tax increase |
| UK | 10-24% on gains | Non-dom abolition compounds the problem |

**The Netherlands case is the most extreme.** The Box 3 reform (effective 2028) will tax crypto holdings at **36% of deemed or actual returns** — including unrealised gains. If you hold EUR 500K in crypto that appreciates by 20%, you owe EUR 36,000 in tax **even if you did not sell a single coin**.

## How Paraguay Solves This

Paraguay offers a clean escape from the DAC8 reporting web:

| Factor | EU (Your Country) | Paraguay |
|---|---|---|
| Crypto capital gains tax | 19-36% depending on country | **0%** (crypto = goods, territorial system) |
| Wealth tax on crypto holdings | Yes (Netherlands 36%, Spain 0.2-3.5%) | **0%** |
| CRS reporting | Yes — full transparency | **No CRS** |
| DAC8 reporting | Yes — exchanges report automatically | **Not in the EU** — no DAC8 |
| Physical presence required | 183 days/year | **1 visit every 3 years** |
| Citizenship | Your country | **3 years** |

Paraguay classifies crypto as "goods" for natural persons under its tax code. This means:

- Buying and selling crypto is **not a taxable event** (you are trading goods, not securities)
- Capital gains on crypto are **0%** under the territorial system
- There is **no wealth tax** on crypto holdings
- Paraguay does **not participate in CRS** — your crypto stays private
- Paraguay is **not in the EU** — DAC8 does not apply

## But What About DNIT Resolution 47/2026?

In March 2026, Paraguay's tax authority (DNIT) introduced a new resolution requiring certain taxpayers to disclose their crypto holdings.

This is **critical to understand**: Resolution 47/2026 is a **reporting obligation**, not a **tax**. Paraguay is not taxing your crypto. They are simply asking for disclosure to monitor for money laundering and terrorist financing — standard international practice.

Compare this to your EU country: your government taxes your crypto AND receives full DAC8 reports. Paraguay just asks you to file a form, without taxing the gains.

## The Numbers

Italian crypto investor with EUR 200K in crypto, earning 15% annual gains:

**Stay in Italy (2026+):**
- Capital gains tax (33%): EUR 9,900/year
- DAC8 reporting: full transparency to Agenzia delle Entrate
- Wealth tax (IVAFE 0.2%): EUR 400/year
- **Total: EUR 10,300/year in tax**

**Move to Paraguay:**
- Capital gains tax: **EUR 0**
- Wealth tax: **EUR 0**
- Reporting: simple annual form to DNIT — not a tax
- **Total: EUR 0 in tax**

**Annual saving: EUR 10,300. Lifetime: EUR 300,000+ over a 30-year horizon.**

## Crypto-Friendly Banking in Paraguay

| Service | Type | Details |
|---|---|---|
| **X4T** | Licensed crypto exchange | Paraguay-licensed, bank-integrated |
| **Ueno** | Digital bank | Crypto-friendly, English app |
| **Oobit** | Crypto payments | Spend crypto directly |
| **Schwab International** | US brokerage | Accessible from PY |

## Next Steps

If you hold meaningful crypto assets and are a tax resident of an EU country, DAC8 changes your calculus. The window to restructure your residency before your 2026 DAC8 report hits your tax authority's inbox is closing.

We work with crypto investors regularly. Our team understands the specific needs: 0% CGT jurisdiction, no CRS, no wealth tax, and a jurisdiction that treats crypto as property, not a security.

posts.title: FEIE + Paraguay: How Americans Can Earn Up to $132,900 Tax-Free in 2026
posts.excerpt: The Foreign Earned Income Exclusion lets US citizens exclude up to $132,900 of foreign-earned income from US tax. Combined with Paraguay's 0% territorial tax, the result is a near-zero effective tax rate for American expats. Here is how it works.
posts.author: Nexa Paraguay
posts.content:
Americans living abroad face a unique problem: the US taxes your worldwide income regardless of where you live. It is called citizenship-based taxation, and only two countries in the world do it (the US and Eritrea).

But there is a powerful tool designed exactly for this situation: the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE). And when you pair it with Paraguay's territorial tax system, you can earn up to **$132,900 completely tax-free** — no US tax, no Paraguay tax, no tax anywhere.

## How FEIE Works

The FEIE (Section 911 of the Internal Revenue Code) allows US citizens and resident aliens to exclude foreign-earned income from US taxation. For 2026, the exclusion is **$132,900**.

To qualify, you must pass one of two tests:

**Bona Fide Residence Test:** You are a bona fide resident of a foreign country for an uninterrupted period that includes a full tax year.

**Physical Presence Test:** You are physically present in a foreign country for at least 330 days in any 12-month period.

If you qualify, the first $132,900 of your foreign-earned income is exempt from US federal income tax. You still need to file (Form 2555), but you pay zero on that income.

## The Paraguay Advantage

Here is the critical part: FEIE exempts you from **US** tax on foreign income. But you still need to live somewhere that does not tax that income either. Otherwise, you just shift your tax burden from the IRS to a foreign government.

That is where Paraguay comes in.

| Scenario | US Tax | Local Tax | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live in Spain (NLV) | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 47% + wealth tax | **Up to $62,000** |
| Live in Portugal D7 | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 48% (post-NHR) | **Up to $63,000** |
| Live in Costa Rica | $0 (FEIE) | 0% foreign income, 15% local | **$0 (if income is foreign)** |
| Live in Thailand | $0 (FEIE) | Up to 35% if remitted | **Up to $46,500** |
| **Live in Paraguay** | **$0 (FEIE)** | **0% on foreign income** | **$0** |

**Paraguay is the only jurisdiction that completes the full stack: FEIE + 0% local tax + no wealth tax + no CRS + citizenship in 3 years.**

## How It Works Step by Step

1. **Establish foreign tax residence** in Paraguay. This requires physical presence (bona fide residence test) or 330 days (physical presence test). Paraguay's process is straightforward — 60-90 days to temporary residency.

2. **Earn income through a foreign structure** or as an independent contractor. FEIE covers employee compensation and self-employment income earned outside the US.

3. **File Form 2555** with your US tax return. Claim the FEIE on your foreign-earned income up to $132,900.

4. **Pay zero Paraguay tax** on that income. Paraguay's territorial system taxes only Paraguay-source income. Your US-earned or internationally-earned income is 0% taxed in Paraguay.

5. **File FBAR and FATCA** as required. Paraguay does not participate in CRS, but US citizens must still report foreign accounts.

## The Numbers

American freelancer earning $120,000/year working remotely from Asunción:

**Living in the US:**
- Federal income tax: ~$18,000
- Self-employment tax: ~$16,000
- State tax (e.g., California): ~$6,000
- **Total: ~$40,000**

**Living in Paraguay (FEIE + territorial):**
- US federal tax: **$0** (FEIE covers $120K)
- Self-employment tax: **$0** (FEIE applies to SE income with proper structure)
- Paraguay tax: **$0** (foreign income)
- **Total: ~$0**

**Annual saving: $40,000.**

## What About Income Over $132,900?

If you earn more than the FEIE threshold, the excess is still subject to US tax. However:

- The Foreign Tax Credit can offset US tax on excess income if you pay tax to Paraguay — but you won't, because Paraguay taxes local income at 10%
- Consider splitting income: $132,900 through FEIE, remaining through a foreign corporation taxed at Paraguay's 10% corporate rate
- Paraguay's 10% corporate rate is lower than US rates for most earners

## What About FBAR and FATCA?

As a US citizen, you must report foreign bank accounts (FBAR) and specified foreign financial assets (FATCA Form 8938). Paraguay is not a CRS participant, meaning your Paraguay bank accounts are not automatically reported to the IRS.

You still must file these forms voluntarily. But the compliance burden is straightforward — file the forms annually with your tax return.

## What About State Taxes?

If you establish residency in a state with no income tax (Texas, Florida, Nevada, etc.) before moving, state tax is not an issue. If you move directly from California or New York, those states may try to assert continued residency.

**Planning tip:** Establish a domicile in a no-tax state (get a driver's license, register to vote, lease an address) before leaving the US for Paraguay.

## The Bigger Picture

There are 5.5 million Americans living abroad. The number of US citizenship renunciations hit record highs in 2025 (over 6,000 projected). The trend is clear: more Americans are leaving, and those who leave want a jurisdiction that respects the fact that their income is earned outside that country.

Paraguay is the only country that combines:
- **0% foreign income tax** (territorial system)
- **No wealth tax**
- **No inheritance tax**
- **No CRS reporting**
- **Citizenship in 3 years**
- **Cost of living 60-70% lower than the US**

## Next Steps

We help Americans structure their Paraguay residency correctly — including navigating the FEIE qualification requirements, setting up proper business structures, and ensuring FBAR/FATCA compliance.

items.q: How long does the whole process take?
items.a: In-person in one day. Issuance: 45–60 days. Company + bank: 2–4 weeks. Total: 8–12 weeks.

items.q: How many trips do I need?
items.a: One trip is sufficient.

items.q: What does the price include?
items.a: Professional fees, VAT, official taxes, bank coordination, real-estate tour and integrated advisory. No additional fees.

items.q: What is NOT included?
items.a: International flights, accommodation, personal expenses, sworn translations and apostilles in your country of origin.

items.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
items.a: No. Our team accompanies you and communicates in Dutch, English and German.

items.q: Can a foreigner open a bank account?
items.a: Yes. It is the most complex step; we prepare your financial profile and coordinate directly with the bank.

items.q: What type of company is incorporated?
items.a: Our legal team recommends the most suitable structure (typically EAS or SA).

items.q: Is the process 100% legal?
items.a: Absolutely. Strict adherence to Paraguayan and international regulations.

items.q: What if a document is missing?
items.a: We detect it before your trip. Our pre-validation ensures you arrive fully prepared.

items.q: Do you guarantee bank approval?
items.a: The decision is the bank's. We guarantee professional preparation and institutional coordination.

items.q: Can I bring my family?
items.a: Yes. Each family member requires their own residency process.

items.q: How is payment made?
items.a: Upfront by bank transfer. No additional fees.

items.q: Can I get only the residency?
items.a: Programs are integrated by design. Contact us for your specific case.

items.q: What happens after year one (Investor)?
items.a: We present a continuation proposal tailored to your needs.

items.q: What if laws change during my process?
items.a: We monitor the regulatory environment and inform you immediately of any relevant changes.

items.q: Permanent residency
items.a: Permanent migratory status in Paraguay. Obtained through an 8–12 week process from a complete file submission.

items.q: Cédula de Identidad
items.a: Paraguayan ID card issued after residency is granted. Official document for in-country operations.

items.q: RUC
items.a: Unique Taxpayer Registry. Tax identifier equivalent to a NIF or BTW number.

items.q: 10 % IRE
items.a: Corporate income tax. General rate on income generated in Paraguay.

items.q: Territoriality
items.a: Tax system taxing only income generated within the country. Foreign income pays no IRE.

items.q: SEPRELAD
items.a: Paraguay's anti-money-laundering authority. Nexa is a reporting entity, which means strict KYC.

items.q: KYC
items.a: Know Your Customer. Identity and source-of-funds verification required to operate legally.

items.q: What does the price include?
items.a: Fees, VAT, official taxes, bank coordination and integrated advisory.

items.q: What is NOT included?
items.a: Flights, accommodation, apostilles in country of origin, personal expenses.

items.q: How is payment made?
items.a: Upfront by wire transfer. No additional fees.

items.q: Can I switch programs after starting?
items.a: Yes. If mid-process you decide to upgrade (e.g. from Base to Business) we roll the paid amount into the new program and invoice the delta. No double fees.

items.q: Do I need to be in Paraguay to start?
items.a: No. We handle document pre-validation remotely. You only travel for the single operational day (migration + cédula + bank, all coordinated).

items.q: How long does the whole process take end-to-end?
items.a: 8–12 weeks typical. 6 weeks document prep + 1 trip + 2–4 weeks for residency approval + cédula issuance.

items.q: What happens if my residency is rejected?
items.a: Rejections are rare with proper document prep. If it happens for a reason within our scope (e.g. missed requirement) we re-present at our cost.

items.q: Is the 10% territorial tax guaranteed?
items.a: The 10% IRE rate is current Paraguayan law (Ley 6380). We keep you updated on any reforms and structure your setup to stay compliant under the rules that apply at the time.

bank-account.fullDescription: We prepare your financial profile, select the right bank for your needs, coordinate appointments, and accompany you through the account opening process. Our institutional relationships with major Paraguayan banks help streamline what is often the most complex step for foreigners.

cedula.fullDescription: We guide you through every step of obtaining your Paraguayan national ID card. From scheduling your appointment to accompanying you on the day, we ensure you have all required documentation and that the process is completed smoothly.

due-diligence.fullDescription: We conduct comprehensive due diligence on any property you intend to rent or buy. This includes title verification, lien checks, tax status confirmation, zoning compliance assessment, and historical ownership review. We ensure your investment is safe before you commit.

property-purchase.fullDescription: We provide expert assistance throughout the property buying process — from identifying investment opportunities to closing the deal. Our team includes legal professionals who verify titles, coordinate with notaries, and ensure your investment is protected under Paraguayan law.

rentals.fullDescription: We help you find high-quality rental properties that match your lifestyle and budget. Whether you need a furnished apartment for a short-term stay or a family home for long-term residence, we navigate the local market, arrange viewings, and assist with lease negotiations.

ruc.fullDescription: We handle your registration with the Subsecretaría de Estado de Tributación (SET) to obtain your RUC.
